rule.name: R-3
rule.description: All functions shall have a cyclomatic complexity number of 20 or less.

rule.name: A-1
rule.description: Any one function (or method) will contain no more than 200 logical source lines of code (L-SLOCs).

section.name: Environment

rule.name: R-8
rule.description: All code shall conform to ISO/IEC 14882:2002(E) standard C++.

rule.name: R-14
rule.description: Literal suffixes shall use uppercase rather than lowercase letters.

rule.name: R-15
rule.description: Provision shall be made for run-time checking (defensive programming).

section.rules: <rule name="A-12" enable="1" level="0" checker="" description="The following digraphs will not be used: <%, %>, <:, :>, %:, %:%:." expand="0"/>

section.name: Libraries
section.rules:
<rule name="R-18" enable="1" level="1" checker="" description="The macro offsetof, in library , shall not be used." expand="0"/> <rule name="R-19" enable="1" level="1" checker="" description=" and the setlocale function shall not be used." expand="0"/>
<rule name="R-21" enable="1" level="1" checker="" description="The signal handling facilities of shall not be used." expand="0"/> <rule name="R-22" enable="1" level="1" checker="" description="The input/output library shall not be used." expand="0"/> <rule name="R-23" enable="1" level="1" checker="" description="The library functions atof, atoi and atol from library shall not be used." expand="0"/> <rule name="R-24" enable="1" level="1" checker="" description="The library functions abort, exit, getenv and system from library shall not be used." expand="0"/> <rule name="R-25" enable="1" level="1" checker="" description="The time handling functions of library shall not be used." expand="0"/>

rule.name: R-26
rule.description: Only the following preprocessor directives shall be used: #ifndef, #define, #endif, #include.

rule.name: R-29
rule.description: The #define preprocessor directive shall not be used to create inline macros. Inline functions shall be used instead.

rule.name: R-30
rule.description: The #define preprocessor directive shall not be used to define constant values. Instead, the const qualifier shall be applied to variable declarations to specify constant values.

rule.name: A-27
rule.description: #ifndef, #define and #endif will be used to prevent multiple inclusions of the same header file. Other techniques to prevent the multiple inclusions of header files will not be used.

rule.name: A-28
rule.description: The #ifndef and #endif preprocessor directives will only be used as defined in AV Rule 27 to prevent multiple inclusions of the same header file.

rule.name: A-31
rule.description: The #define preprocessor directive will only be used as part of the technique to prevent multiple inclusions of the same header file.

rule.name: A-32
rule.description: The #include preprocessor directive will only be used to include header (*.h) files.

section.name: Header Files
section.rules: <rule name="R-33" enable="1" level="1" checker="external" description="The #include directive shall use the notation to include header files." expand="0"/>

rule.name: A-35
rule.description: A header file will contain a mechanism that prevents multiple inclusions of itself.

rule.name: A-39
rule.description: Header files (*.h) will not contain non-const variable definitions or function definitions.

rule.name: R-40
rule.description: Every implementation file shall include the header files that uniquely define the inline functions, types, and templates used.

rule.name: R-43
rule.description: Tabs should be avoided.

rule.name: R-52
rule.description: Identifiers for constant and enumerator values shall be lowercase.

rule.name: R-59
rule.description: The statements forming the body of an if, else if, else, while, do ... while or for statement shall always be enclosed in braces, even if the braces form an empty block.

rule.name: A-41
rule.description: Source lines will be kept to a length of 120 characters or less.

rule.name: A-42
rule.description: Each expression-statement will be on a separate line.

rule.name: A-44
rule.description: All indentations will be at least two spaces and be consistent within the same source file.

rule.name: A-46
rule.description: User-specified identifiers (internal and external) will not rely on significance of more than 64 characters.

rule.name: A-47
rule.description: Identifiers will not begin with the underscore character '_'.

rule.name: A-48
rule.description: Identifiers will not differ by:Only a mixture of case The presence/absence of the underscore character The interchange of the letter 'O'; with the number '0' or the letter 'D' The interchange of the letter 'I'; with the number '1' or the letter 'l' The interchange of the letter 'S' with the number '5' The interchange of the letter 'Z' with the number 2 The interchange of the letter 'n' with the letter 'h'

rule.name: A-50
rule.description: The first word of the name of a class, structure, namespace, enumeration, or type created with typedef will begin with an uppercase letter. All others letters will be lowercase.

rule.name: A-51
rule.description: All letters contained in function and variables names will be composed entirely of lowercase letters.

rule.name: A-53
rule.description: Header files will always have file name extension of ".h".

rule.name: A-53.1
rule.description: The following character sequences shall not appear in header file names: ', \, /*, //, or "."

rule.name: A-54
rule.description: Implementation files will always have a file name extension of ".cpp".

rule.name: A-57
rule.description: The public, protected, and private sections of a class will be declared in that order.

rule.name: A-58
rule.description: When declaring and defining functions with more than two parameters, the leading parenthesis and the first argument will be written on the same line as the function name. Each additional argument will be written on a separate line (with the closing parenthesis directly after the last argument).

rule.name: A-60
rule.description: Braces ("{}") which enclose a block will be placed in the same column, on separate lines directly before and after the block.

rule.name: A-61
rule.description: Braces ("{}") which enclose a block will have nothing else on the line except comments.

rule.name: A-62
rule.description: The dereference operator ‘*’ and the address-of operator ‘&’ will be directly connected with the type-specifier.

rule.name: A-63
rule.description: Spaces will not be used around ‘.’ or ‘->’, nor between unary operators and operands.

rule.name: R-67
rule.description: Public and protected data should only be used in structs - not classes.

rule.name: R-68
rule.description: Unneeded implicitly generated member functions shall be explicitly disallowed.

rule.name: R-71
rule.description: A class’s virtual functions shall not be invoked from its destructor or any of its constructors.

rule.name: R-75
rule.description: Members of the initialization list shall be listed in the order in which they are declared in the class.

rule.name: R-76
rule.description: A copy constructor and an assignment operator shall be declared for classes that contain pointers to data items or nontrivial destructors.

rule.name: R-77
rule.description: The definition of a member function shall not contain default arguments that produce a signature identical to that of the implicitly-declared copy constructor for the corresponding class/structure.

rule.name: R-78
rule.description: All base classes with a virtual function shall define a virtual destructor.

rule.name: R-79
rule.description: All resources acquired by a class shall be released by the class’s destructor.

rule.name: R-81
rule.description: The assignment operator shall handle self-assignment correctly

rule.name: R-82
rule.description: An assignment operator shall return a reference to *this.

rule.name: R-83
rule.description: An assignment operator shall assign all data members and bases that affect the class invariant (a data element representing a cache, for example, would not need to be copied).

rule.name: R-88
rule.description: Multiple inheritance shall only be allowed in the following restricted form: n interfaces plus m private implementations, plus at most one protected implementation.

rule.name: R-88.1
rule.description: A stateful virtual base shall be explicitly declared in each derived class that accesses it.

rule.name: R-89
rule.description: A base class shall not be both virtual and nonvirtual in the same hierarchy.

rule.name: R-94
rule.description: An inherited nonvirtual function shall not be redefined in a derived class.

rule.name: R-95
rule.description: An inherited default parameter shall never be redefined.

rule.name: R-96
rule.description: Arrays shall not be treated polymorphically.

rule.name: R-97
rule.description: Arrays shall not be used in interface.

rule.name: R-97.1
rule.description: Neither operand of an equality operator (== or !=) shall be a pointer to a virtual member function.

rule.name: R-100
rule.description: Elements from a namespace should be selected as follows:1.using declaration or explicit qualification for few (approximately five) names,2.using directive for many names.

rule.name: R-101
rule.description: Templates shall be reviewed as follows:1.with respect to the template in isolation considering assumptions or requirements placed on its arguments.2.with respect to all functions instantiated by actual arguments.

rule.name: R-102
rule.description: Template tests shall be created to cover all actual template instantiations.

rule.name: R-103
rule.description: Constraint checks should be applied to template arguments.

rule.name: R-105
rule.description: A template definition’s dependence on its instantiation contexts should be minimized.

rule.name: R-106
rule.description: Specializations for pointer types should be made where appropriate.

rule.name: R-112
rule.description: Function return values should not obscure resource ownership.

rule.name: R-118.1
rule.description: Arguments should be passed via pointers if NULL values are possible, An object should be passed as const T* if its value should not be modified.

rule.name: R-118.2
rule.description: Arguments should be passed via pointers if NULL values are possible, An object should be passed as T* if its value may be modified.

rule.name: R-120
rule.description: Overloaded operations or methods should form families that use the same semantics, share the same name, have the same purpose, and that are differentiated by formal parameters.

rule.name: R-123
rule.description: The number of accessor and mutator functions should be minimized.

rule.name: R-124
rule.description: Trivial forwarding functions should be inlined.

rule.name: R-125
rule.description: Unnecessary temporary objects should be avoided.

rule.name: A-115
rule.description: If a function returns error information, then that error information will be tested.

rule.name: R-129
rule.description: Comments in header files should describe the externally visible behavior of the functions or classes being documented.

rule.name: R-130
rule.description: The purpose of every line of executable code should be explained by a comment, although one comment may describe more than one line of code.

rule.name: R-134
rule.description: Assumptions (limitations) made by functions should be documented in the function’s preamble.

rule.name: A-128
rule.description: Comments that document actions or sources (e.g. tables, figures, paragraphs, etc.) outside of the file being documented will not be allowed.

rule.name: A-131
rule.description: One should avoid stating in comments what is better stated in code (i.e. do not simply repeat what is in the code).

rule.name: A-132
rule.description: Each variable declaration, typedef, enumeration value, and structure member will be commented.

rule.name: A-143
rule.description: Variables will not be introduced until they can be initialized with meaningful values.(See also AV Rule 136, AV Rule 142, and AV Rule 73 concerning declaration scope, initialization before use, and default constructors respectively.)

rule.name: R-146
rule.description: Floating point implementations shall comply with a defined floating point standard. The standard that will be used is the ANSI®/IEEE® Std 754 [1].

rule.name: A-155
rule.description: Bit-fields will not be used to pack data into a word for the sole purpose of saving space.

rule.name: R-167
rule.description: The implementation of integer division in the chosen compiler shall be determined, documented and taken into account.

rule.name: R-183
rule.description: Every possible measure should be taken to avoid type casting.

rule.name: R-204
rule.description: A single operation with side-effects shall only be used in the following contexts:1.by itself 2.the right-hand side of an assignment 3.a condition 4.the only argument expression with a side-effect in a function call 5.condition of a loop 6.switch condition 7. single part of a chained operation

rule.name: A-207
rule.description: Unencapsulated global data will be avoided.

rule.name: R-210
rule.description: Algorithms shall not make assumptions concerning how data is represented in memory (e.g. big endian vs. little endian, base class subobject ordering in derived classes, nonstatic data member ordering across access specifiers, etc.).

rule.name: R-210.1
rule.description: Algorithms shall not make assumptions concerning the order of allocation of nonstatic data members separated by an access specifier.

rule.name: R-211
rule.description: Algorithms shall not assume that shorts, ints, longs, floats, doubles or long doubles begin at particular addresses.

rule.name: R-212
rule.description: Underflow or overflow functioning shall not be depended on in any special way.

rule.name: R-214
rule.description: Assuming that non-local static objects, in separate translation units, are initialized in a special order shall not be done.

rule.name: R-216
rule.description: Programmers should not attempt to prematurely optimize code.

rule.name: R-217
rule.description: Compile-time and link-time errors should be preferred over run-time errors.

rule.name: A-218
rule.description: Compiler warning levels will be set in compliance with project policies.

rule.name: R-219
rule.description: All tests applied to a base class interface shall be applied to all derived class interfaces as well. If the derived class poses stronger postconditions/invariants, then the new postconditions /invariants shall be substituted in the derived class tests.

rule.name: R-220
rule.description: Structural coverage algorithms shall be applied against flattened classes.

rule.name: R-221
rule.description: Structural coverage of a class within an inheritance hierarchy containing virtual functions shall include testing every possible resolution for each set of identical polymorphic references.
